controls.reason: The statement requires an explicit mandatory-or-optional classification for procedure steps, which a closed versioned step schema decides exactly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an untyped step, a third ambiguous type, and prose guidance linked to no step; exact inventory and two-value enum checks fail each. Whether the steps are wise is outside the claim.

controls.reason: A nonempty purpose and hazard field does not establish that the text truthfully explains the step's purpose or the hazard it controls.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical shutdown step says purpose `required` and hazard `bad outcome`. All record fields pass, but personnel receive no actual explanation of purpose or controlled hazard.

controls.reason: The claim is training occurrence across four explicitly named non-routine condition classes; bound curricula, participants, and authenticated completions decide it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried routine-only attendance relabelled emergency, omitted recovery training, and completion for another role revision; scenario taxonomy and joins fail each. Competence is not asserted.

controls.reason: Which system, threat, procedure, or role changes are material requires judgment, and change and training inventories can omit a triggering change.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A new attack technique makes the response procedure obsolete but is labelled nonmaterial and excluded from refresh. Every declared material change has later training, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Proving simulations cannot affect any production user or data requires complete inventories of credentials, endpoints, integrations, copies, queues, and indirect side effects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A drill sends test notifications through an unlisted production provider credential. All declared practice environments are isolated, so evidence joins pass while production users are affected.

controls.reason: The statement asks whether four named subjects are included in exercise evidence, which a bound plan and authenticated execution record can prove.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a communications-only plan, an exercise with no evidence-preservation event, and customer impact from another drill; exact four-topic and exercise-ID joins fail each. Quality is not claimed.

controls.reason: A record of observed assistance cannot prove that a human participant received no undocumented help through an unobserved channel.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The protocol record can say no assistance while an observer gives off-record help, so complete record fields pass without proving the negative human-behavior claim.

controls.reason: Inclusion in evaluation is a bounded participation fact, not an accessibility-outcome claim; privacy-preserving authenticated study evidence can prove it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a consultation outside the tool evaluation, a participant record with no valid inclusion evidence, and an evaluation of a noncritical revision; subject and participant bindings reject each.

controls.reason: Record fields cannot establish that selected tasks, roles, environments, data, devices, and stress conditions are representative of real operation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A high-end desktop, expert operator, clean data, and calm office are labelled representative for emergency field work. Every field exists while the evaluation remains unrealistic.

controls.reason: Six attachments or method labels do not prove the evidence was meaningfully combined into one coherent human-factors evaluation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A case links unrelated interviews, metrics, and logs under the six required labels but never analyzes them together. The schema passes although the methods are not combined.

controls.reason: Exact deployed interface and configuration identifiers can be joined to authenticated critical-task evaluation evidence, making this environment-binding fact bounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a screenshot lookalike, the right interface with staging flags, and a production digest from after the study; artifact, configuration, and time bindings fail each. Human performance quality is separate.

controls.reason: A deviation register cannot independently prove it contains every difference between test conditions and real operation across people, workload, data, environment, and timing.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The test uses expert daytime staff while real work uses novices overnight, but that difference is omitted. Every recorded deviation has complete fields, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: `Major` change applicability and meaningful human-performance re-evaluation require contextual judgment, while change inventories can omit staffing and process changes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Automation removes a verification step but is labelled minor, so no re-evaluation occurs. Every declared major change has an evaluation record, and the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Configured metrics do not prove complete or meaningful monitoring of near misses, recovery, abandonment, and support demand across all channels.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Near misses reported verbally and recoveries performed offline never enter telemetry, while the six configured dashboards remain active. The record check passes despite missing real signals.

controls.reason: The register cannot prove every human-factors risk was recognized, and classifying unresolved risks and adequate monitoring requires specialist judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A confusing emergency control creates a serious risk but is absent from the register. Every listed unresolved risk has owner, monitor, and expiry, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Whether human error could cause catastrophic or systemic harm is a safety judgment over an incomplete hazard inventory, not a deterministic review trigger.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dosing-interface error can harm many patients but is classified noncatastrophic and omitted from independent review. Every declared high-impact subject has a reviewer, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The rule is an inclusion requirement: exact assurance-case identifiers can be joined to authenticated human-factors evidence artifacts and their revisions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a broken link, evidence from another release, and a readiness case with no human-factors artifact; integrity and scope joins fail each. Whether the evidence supports release is not asserted.
